key_insight: A surrogate modeling strategy that remains accurate across different numerical grid resolutions enables fast, reliable prediction of rock–fluid interaction without the need for costly high-resolution PDE solves.
problem_solved: High-fidelity numerical models for coupled rock–fluid interaction require very fine spatial resolution, making repeated runs (for uncertainty quantification, optimization, or design) computationally prohibitive.
method: Develop a grid-size-invariant surrogate model trained on multi-resolution simulation data so it generalizes across discretizations without retraining for each grid.
Incorporate interface-aware physics constraints and/or PDE-consistent losses to preserve key reaction and flow behaviors at rock–fluid boundaries.
Use dimensionality reduction / operator-style learning to map inputs (geometry, boundary conditions, properties) to outputs (flow fields, reaction rates) efficiently for many-query tasks.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a way to replace expensive PDE solvers by a fast, generalizable surrogate that supports large-scale uncertainty quantification, optimization, and real-time decision-making in subsurface and geoscience applications.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: high-fidelity PDE solver (dense grid, slow) vs. surrogate model (coarse or variable grid, fast) with timing and accuracy callouts.
Flowchart of the training pipeline showing multi-resolution data input → grid-size-invariant model → predictions on unseen grid sizes.
Heatmaps or contour plots comparing predicted vs. reference flow/reaction fields across different grid resolutions with error overlays.
Bar chart or log plot of compute cost (runtime or FLOPs) vs. accuracy for high-fidelity solver and surrogate across multiple scenarios.
paper_title: Surrogate models for Rock-Fluid Interaction: A Grid-Size-Invariant Approach
paper_authors: Nathalie C. Pinheiro, Donghu Guo, Hannah P. Menke, Aniket C. Joshi, Claire E. Heaney
